summary: Specifies the IP Flow Information Export (IPFIX) protocol for sending traffic flow information from an exporting process to a collecting process. It defines how data and template records are carried, so the data format is described with it. It was replaced by RFC 7011.

eli5.summary: Routers count what traffic passes through them and send summary reports to a collector. IPFIX is the format and way of delivering those reports. It was replaced by RFC 7011.

questions: how are ip flow records exported
subtitle: How routers and probes ship summaries of the traffic they have seen to a collector, using self-describing templates.

tldr.problem: Network devices can observe IP traffic flows, but every vendor reported them in its own way, so a collector could not receive flow information from many devices in a uniform form.
tldr.mechanism: IPFIX sends flow information in messages made of sets. Template records describe the layout of fields, and data records carry the values. Messages travel over SCTP (required), and optionally UDP or TCP.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5101 was obsoleted by RFC 7011, which is the current IPFIX protocol specification.

today: RFC 5101 is a Proposed Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 7011, so new work should use that specification instead.

sections.title: Why a Flow Export Protocol
sections.content:
A data network mostly consists of IP flows passing through network elements. A Flow is defined as a set of IP packets passing an Observation Point during a certain time interval, where all packets share a set of common properties, such as the destination address or destination port.

Administrators often want information about these flows. A Collecting Process should be able to receive it from many network elements, which requires a uniform way of representing flow information and of sending it. RFC 5101 specifies that protocol: the representation of flows, the extra data needed to interpret them, the packet format, the transport mechanisms and the security concerns.

The work is split across documents. The architecture is in a separate document, and the formal description of the Information Elements (the named attributes that can appear in a record) is in RFC 5102.
sections.eli5: Many routers see lots of traffic. They all need to report it in the same format, or the person reading the reports would get confused.

sections.title: Exporters, Collectors and Records
sections.content:
A Metering Process generates Flow Records from packets seen at an Observation Point. An Exporting Process, hosted on an Exporter, sends those records to one or more Collecting Processes on a Collector. The Observation Domain is the largest set of Observation Points whose Flow information can be aggregated by a Metering Process, and it has an ID that is unique per Exporting Process.

A Template is an ordered sequence of type and length pairs that completely specifies the structure and meaning of a set of information. Each Template has a Template ID. A Data Record holds the values that match a Template Record, so a collector can read a record only when it has the matching template.

A Flow Key is a field used to define a Flow, for example a destination IP address.
sections.eli5: A template is the column headings of a table, and a data record is one row of numbers. You need the headings first, or the numbers mean nothing.

sections.title: The IPFIX Message, Sets and Records
sections.content:
An IPFIX Message is a Message Header followed by one or more Sets. There are three kinds of Set: Template Set, Options Template Set and Data Set. Record types MUST NOT be mixed within a Set. All binary integers are in network byte order (big-endian).

The Message Header carries a Version (0x000a), the Length of the whole message in octets, the Export Time in seconds since 1 January 1970 UTC, a Sequence Number and a 32-bit Observation Domain ID. The Sequence Number counts Data Records, not messages, and lets a collector notice missed records.

Each Set begins with a Set Header of Set ID and Length. A Set ID of 2 means a Template Set and 3 means an Options Template Set. Values above 255 are Data Sets, and the Set ID of a Data Set is the Template ID of the template that describes its records.

A Template Record lists Field Specifiers. Each has an Enterprise bit, an Information Element identifier and a Field Length. If the Enterprise bit is 1, a four-octet Enterprise Number follows, which lets vendors define their own elements. Template IDs for data run from 256 to 65535.

An Options Template adds a scope, which says what the reported values apply to (for example a particular template or interface). Its Scope Field Count MUST NOT be zero.
sections.eli5: A message is an envelope holding labelled bundles. One kind of bundle says what the columns are, and another kind holds the numbers.

sections.title: Encoding Values and Variable Lengths
sections.content:
Information Elements are sent in canonical network byte order. Integers use two's complement when signed. Addresses are treated as integers: a MAC address is 6 octets, an IPv4 address 4 octets and an IPv6 address 16 octets. Strings are UTF-8, and floats are IEEE 754 single or double precision.

Reduced-size encoding lets an exporter send an integer in fewer octets than its type implies, if every value it will send still fits. For example, a byte counter defined as 64 bits can be sent as 32 bits by placing a length of 4 instead of 8 in the template. Only leading zeroes are dropped, and signedness is preserved.

For variable-length elements the template gives a field length of 65535. The actual length then travels in the data: one octet if it is below 255, otherwise the octet 255 followed by two octets of length.
sections.eli5: If a number is small, you can write it with fewer digits to save paper. For words of changing length, you write the length first, then the word.

sections.title: Template Management and Transports
sections.content:
An exporter SHOULD send a template before any data that uses it. Templates that are no longer used SHOULD be deleted, and a Template ID MUST NOT be reused before its template is deleted. Over SCTP and TCP, deletion is done with a Template Withdrawal Message, which is a template record with a Field Count of 0. A suggested default delay before withdrawing is 5 seconds after the last Data Record.

A compliant implementation MUST support SCTP with the PR-SCTP extension. UDP and TCP MAY also be implemented. The default port is 4739, and 4740 is the default for secure connections, in each case for SCTP, UDP and TCP.

UDP is not reliable, so it MUST NOT be used unless some loss of messages is tolerable. Over UDP, templates MUST be re-sent at regular intervals, with a default of 10 minutes, and a collector keeps each template for a lifetime of at least 3 times the refresh timeout. Template Withdrawal Messages MUST NOT be used over UDP. If the path MTU is unknown, UDP messages SHOULD be no larger than 512 octets. An IPFIX Message is at most 65535 octets because of its 16-bit Length field.

Section 4 also defines optional Options Templates for reporting statistics about the Metering Process and Exporting Process, and for reporting a template's Flow Keys.
sections.eli5: You send the column headings before the numbers. Over an unreliable path you repeat the headings now and then in case one got lost.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
IPFIX data can be used for network forensics and billing, and it can reveal network configuration and user traffic, so confidentiality, integrity and authentication are required. An attacker injecting false messages could falsify data or change or revoke templates at the collector.

The RFC requires DTLS for SCTP and for UDP, and TLS for TCP. The exporter acts as the client and the collector as the server, and both sides MUST use strong mutual authentication with X.509 certificates, checking the peer's fully qualified domain name.

The RFC also discusses denial-of-service risks, including state exhaustion at a collector, and suggests rate limits, SYN cookies for TCP, and using a dedicated network. Where TLS or DTLS is not an option, peers can fall back on IP source addresses plus ingress filtering, which is weaker.
sections.eli5: The reports are private and valuable, so both sides check each other's ID and lock the envelope, and the receiver is careful not to be flooded with fake mail.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Total length of the message in octets, including header and Sets.

fields.name: Export Time
fields.desc: Seconds since 0000 UTC Jan 1, 1970 when the header leaves the Exporter.

fields.name: Sequence Number
fields.desc: Running count of Data Records, modulo 2^32.

fields.name: Observation Domain ID
fields.desc: Identifies the Observation Domain that metered the Flows.

fields.name: Set ID
fields.desc: 2 for Template Set, 3 for Options Template Set, above 255 for Data Sets.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Total length of the Set in octets, including the Set Header, records and padding.
